text: [V] a competing driver documents that on Workers TLS options are ignored and `channel_binding=require` is unavailable; whether that is a platform limit is FS-04's question.
[V] Workers: no socket at global scope; connection-count limits apply; TLS options and channel binding are constrained.
connect() accepts either a SocketAddress object with hostname and port or a single string, plus an optional SocketOptions object, and returns a Socket.
SocketOptions.secureTransport takes "off", "on" or "starttls" and defaults to "off"; "on" starts TLS when the socket is created.
The documented SocketOptions members are only secureTransport and allowHalfOpen; no certificate, CA, SNI or expected-hostname option is documented for connect() or startTls().
startTls() can be called only on a socket created with secureTransport set to "starttls".
startTls() returns a new Socket, the original socket can no longer be read or written, and startTls() should be called once per socket.
allowHalfOpen defaults to false, which closes the writable side automatically at end-of-file; true keeps the writable side open after EOF.

socket.opened resolves with SocketInfo (remoteAddress and localAddress, each possibly undefined) once connected and rejects on error; socket.closed resolves when the socket closes and rejects on error.
The socket's WritableStream accepts only Uint8Array chunks or views of them.
Outbound connect() to Cloudflare IP ranges is refused.
A TCP socket cannot be created in global scope and shared across requests; connect() during global scope fails with a disallowed-operation error.
Each open TCP socket counts toward the maximum number of simultaneously open connections.
Outbound connect() to port 25 is refused with the message "Connections to port 25 are prohibited".
connect() to localhost or private network IPs is refused with "proxy request failed, cannot connect to the specified address".
At most six connections per invocation may be waiting for response headers at once, and a seventh attempted while six are waiting is queued rather than rejected.
An I/O object such as a stream created in one request handler cannot be used from another request's handler and raises "Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request".
postgres.js documents that on Workers the server certificate is always verified whatever the ssl option is set to.
postgres.js documents that on Workers channel binding is unavailable because the sockets do not expose the server certificate, so channel_binding 'require' is rejected with CHANNEL_BINDING_REQUIRED.
postgres.js documents that on Workers sslnegotiation 'direct' is refused because Workers sockets cannot send ALPN.
postgres.js documents that a Workers TLS handshake fails, most often when the server certificate is not signed by a publicly trusted CA, and surfaces this as TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.
